items.h: Snags late catch in Thanksgiving loss
items.s: Allen caught his lone target for 19 yards during the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday. Allen's 23 offensive snaps were third most on the Chiefs behind Xavier Worthy (42) and Rashee Rice (38) and ahead of Josh Downs (15). However, Allen didn't see a pass from Patrick Mahomes until midway through the fourth quarter, when the duo connected for a 19-yard gain. Allen, a fifth-round selection of the Chiefs in the 2026 NFL Draft, has accumulated 10 catches on 17 targets for 169 yards and a touchdown over his last seven outings, and he could operate as the WR4 for Week 13 against the Rams on Dec. 3 if Jalen Royals (ankle) cannot play in that contest.

items.h: Cyrus Allen's Playing Time Limits His Week 12 Waiver Appeal
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Cyrus Allen topped 40 receiving yards for the second straight game Sunday, even as his playing time fell. The rookie caught two of four targets for 41 yards against the Arizona Cardinals after posting two catches on four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons. Allen played 23 offensive snaps in Atlanta and just 16 against Arizona, the fewest of any Chiefs receiver in the game. Rashee Rice and Josh Downs each drew more targets than Allen in both games, and Kansas City's unofficial depth chart lists him behind Xavier Worthy. I'd leave Allen on waivers in most 12-team redraft leagues. He's a low-priority stash in leagues with 14 or…

Allen caught two of four targets for 41 yards during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals. Allen was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after having done so only twice in the team's first eight games of the year. The wide receiver played 16 offensive snaps which ranked sixth at his position behind Xavier Worthy (47), Rashee Rice (32), Jalen Royals (24), Andrew Armstrong (20) and Josh Downs (17). As a result of the depth of the WR room in Kansas City, Allen will remain a hard fantasy option to trust Thursday versus the Bills.

items.h: Cyrus Allen hauls in two passes in Week 11
items.s: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-4 targets for 41 yards in a 34-7 win over Arizona. Allen continues to be used sparingly in the Chiefs' offense, with his four targets tying a season high. Fantasy managers can leave him out of their lineups heading into a Week 12 matchup with the Bills.

items.h: Cyrus Allen Could Operate As A Deep Threat In Week 11
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Cyrus Allen will face the Arizona Cardinals at home in Week 11. Allen finished fourth on the team in yardage last week and was one of four Chiefs pass catchers to walk away with a score. The rookie receiver connected with quarterback Patrick Mahomes for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter of last week's 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Allen's deep ball connection marked the team's first reception of over 30 yards since the loss of Tyquan Thornton to a gruesome ankle injury. With Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice, and Josh Downs all operating more in the short and intermediate parts of the field, Allen could be the pass catcher best suited to operate as…

items.h: Cyrus Allen a Speculative Pickup in Deep Leagues
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Cyrus Allen scored his first NFL touchdown in Week 10, running an impressive route to beat Falcons cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. for a 39-yard score. The rookie set new career highs with four targets and 44 receiving yards as well, and he seems to be finding a nice role in the Chiefs' passing game. Allen played more snaps in Week 10 than both Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals, and he played more than twice as many as newcomer Josh Downs. While Downs works mostly out of the slot, Allen has mostly worked outside so far in his rookie season. He has the potential to be an interesting play down the stretch, but he'll have to beat out Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy…

Allen caught two of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons. The rookie wideout scored his first career touchdown by beating the cornerback on a stutter-go for a 39-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With Josh Downs still getting comfortable and learning the offense following Tuesday's acquisition from the Colts, Allen maintained a significant role on offense, playing 22 of 64 offensive snaps. Once Downs progresses from the 10 snaps he played against Atlanta, it will be interesting to see if Allen can push Xavier Worthy (zero catches on three targets across 56 snaps on Sunday) for a larger piece of the outside receiver role in Kansas City's offense.

items.h: Cyrus Allen reaches end zone in Week 10 win
items.s: Cyrus Allen caught two of his four targets for 44 yards and one touchdown in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons in Week 10. Allen has underwhelmed in the Kansas City offense to this point, recording over 40 receiving yards for the first time in nine contests Sunday. The wideout remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 11 contest against the Arizona Cardinals.

Allen failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets. Allen made the start at wide receiver but ran just 13 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 36 dropbacks against New York. With Xavier Worthy (hamstring) now injured, Allen could have a path to more playing time moving forward, but all three of Rashee Rice, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce are well ahead of the rookie wideout for targets.

items.h: Cyrus Allen Could Earn More Targets In Week 9
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Cyrus Allen caught two of his three targets for 20 yards in last week's loss to the Denver Broncos. Despite the loss, the rookie receiver finished the game fourth on the team in yards. Allen also played his most snaps of the season in Week 8, indicating that the coaching staff is gaining more trust in the young wideout. Given the team's struggles to produce from the wide receiver position, Allen could be the man to step into the WR2 role behind Rashee Rice. It also helps that Allen and Rice win in different areas of the field so the duo could easily coexist. Allen will look to continue his upward trend this Sunday against the New York Jets. The Jets'…

items.h: Two catches in loss to Denver
items.s: Allen caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. The rookie wide receiver usurped Jalen Royals on the depth chart, operating as the clear WR3 behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. Allen ran 22 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 44 dropbacks, but with both Rice and Worthy healthy alongside Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker, there doesn't appear to be much juice to squeeze for Allen.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday that Allen will "get a little bit more [snaps]" during Sunday's game against the Broncos, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports. While the Chiefs have been without top wideout Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) in the past two games, Allen has seen only a modest uptick in playing time. After logging no more than five offensive snaps in each of his first four NFL contests, Allen has played 25 total offensive snaps over the last two weeks while recording three receptions for 45 yards. Even if Reid sticks to his promise to find more work for Allen, it's unclear how much larger his role would grow if Rice is able to put an end to his absence this weekend. Rice…

items.h: Cyrus Allen to See More Snaps in Week 8
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said that rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen will "get a little bit more snaps this week," according to Nate Taylor of ESPN. It is an interesting time for Reid to make this statement with top wideout Rashee Rice potentially returning in Week 8 against the division-rival Denver Broncos on Sunday after missing the team's last two games due to a hamstring injury. Allen played only 15% of the offensive snaps in the Week 6 win over the Los Angeles Chargers and caught both of his targets for 27 yards. While playing a season-high 30% of the snaps in last week's Sunday night loss to the Seattle Seahawks, he caught just one of two targets for 18 yards. The…

items.h: One early catch in Week 7 loss
items.s: Allen caught one of two targets for 18 yards during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Allen and Patrick Mahomes for an 18-yard pass on the Chiefs' second offensive play of the game, but the rookie wide receiver did not see another pass from his veteran quarterback until the fourth quarter. All three of Allen's catches this season have come over his last two games, which has coincided with the absence of Rashee Rice (knee/hamstring). Allen was on the field for 16 of the Chiefs' 53 offensive snaps Sunday, and his minimal role would decrease even more if Rice is cleared to return for Week 8 against the Broncos on Nov. 1.

items.h: Cyrus Allen brings in 18-yard pass in Week 7
items.s: Cyrus Allen caught one of his two targets for an 18-yard gain in a 20-3 loss to the Seahawks in Week 7. Despite an increased role due to injuries, Allen has just three catches for 45 yards over his past two games. The rookie wideout does not need to be rostered in most fantasy leagues heading into Week 8 against the Broncos.

items.h: Cyrus Allen Should See An Uptick In Usage Against Seattle
items.s: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Cyrus Allen will take on the defending Super Bowl champions on the road in Week 7. Allen was listed on the injury report with a knee injury, but practiced fully all week and does not have a designation ahead of the contest. The rookie wideout caught his first career catch against the Los Angeles Chargers last week and displayed his big-play potential. Allen only ran four routes in the game, but earned two targets in his limited time on the field. He turned those two targets into 27 yards and linked up with quarterback Patrick Mahomes to gain a big first down on a crosser. Mahomes displayed trust in the rookie as he dropped in a pass right over a defender…
